full_text_zh:
[P1] 擒贼擒王

[P2] 公元1449年，明英宗忽然接到边关战报，惊得一拍桌子，站了起来。他最信任的宦官王振趁机对他说：‘皇上，这正是您大展拳脚的好机会呀！’

‘启禀皇上，瓦剌太师也先率军攻打大同，参将吴浩战死！’

[P3] 听了王振的话，明英宗做出了一个石破天惊的决定。
"朕要御驾亲征，打败瓦剌！"文武百官听说后，纷纷劝说明英宗不要冒险亲征。

[P4] "皇上，边境战事年年有，只要派兵增援，多多赏赐，一定能打退他们，不需要您御驾亲征呀！"
"皇上，现在天气炎热，草都被晒死了，河水也干了。大军出征在外，人马吃喝都很困难，不是出征的好时候呀！"
"皇上，瓦剌军来得太突然，咱们准备不足，您出征太冒险了！"

[P5] 但是，英宗一心想要建功立业，谁也劝不住他。朝廷上下只好匆忙地准备起来。在大军出发前两天，朝廷给每个士兵发了一两白银，一身棉衣，两双鞋，三斗炒麦；又搬空了武器库，找出八十多万件兵器分发给士兵们。
这么多东西，如果都让士兵背着，就没有办法行军了。于是，朝廷又给每三名士兵配了一头小毛驴。

[P6] 一切准备好了，英宗就带着一百多名文武大臣，率领二十万大军，浩浩荡荡地从北京出发，上前线去了。因为不懂打仗，英宗就把路上行军扎营的事情，都交给了宦官王振来管。不久，大军走到了宣府这个地方。
"轰隆隆——"忽然间，电闪雷鸣，狂风吹得人东倒西歪，豆大的雨点噼噼啪啪砸了下来。

[P7] "皇上，请您在宣府歇息，我们愿领兵出征，赶走瓦剌。"大臣们见天气恶劣，都请求皇帝停止前进。
王振却将他们拦下，怒骂道："边关多次告急，皇上不顾自身安危，带兵亲征，你们不去巡视军营，却要在这里躲风避雨吗？我收到战报，瓦剌人已经退到塞外了，你们赶快去制订作战计划吧！"

[P8] 十几天冒雨行军，大军终于来到大同。可是，这里的战火刚刚熄灭，到处都是战死的士兵和受伤的战马，将士们见了这景象心里不免害怕起来。
这时，大同监军郭敬报告说："瓦剌太师也先故意退兵，就是为了引我们追过去，他们已经在前面埋伏好了，大军再往前就中计了！"

[P9] 而这一夜，大同又下起了暴雨。王振再也不敢往前走，去与瓦剌军交战了。他悄悄地对英宗说："皇上，这一路上，不是刮风就是下雨，天气不好，也不能打仗，还是先班师回朝吧！"英宗见了战场上的尸体，也很害怕，便同意第二天就带兵回京。

[P10] 从大同回北京有两条路，一条是紫荆关，一条是居庸关。王振眼珠一转，笑着对明英宗说："臣的老家在蔚州，如果从紫荆关回京，正好路过，还请皇上赏光，去看一看！"英宗点头说："好，你来安排吧！"

[P11] 第二天，大军一早就向蔚州出发。
可走了没多久，王振又担心起来：
“这么多人去我家，不是要把我田里的庄稼都踩坏了吗？”
“停！停！停！”王振赶紧让队伍停下来，
又劝明英宗说，“臣思来想去，还是要以皇上的安全为重。大军从居庸关回京，才不用担心瓦剌人偷袭呀！”

[P12] 于是，大军又改道向居庸关走去。这一折腾，瓦剌军就从后面追上来了。英宗忙派出四万骑兵阻拦，没想到，四万骑兵都被瓦剌军消灭了。他们只好一面抵抗，一面后退，一直退到了土木堡。土木堡建在一个土坡上，是一个长五百多米、宽一千多米的小城堡。

[P13] 被瓦剌军追赶了好几天，士兵们口渴得像火烧。可是，土木堡里没有井，用水要到十五里外的一条小河去取。那条小河已经被瓦剌军占领了。士兵们想挖一口井，可是向下挖了一米、两米、六七米，却一滴水也没有渗出来。
"大家再忍一忍，明天到了宣府，就有水喝了。"将领们安抚道。

[P14] 第二天，大军正要出发，忽然有士兵来报告："不好，外面有瓦剌军的探子，我们被包围了！" 瓦剌人探得明军人数众多，不久就撤退了。王振听说后，忙命将士们去小河边饮马解渴。士兵们饥渴难耐，争先恐后地往河边跑，乱成了一团。

[P15] 就在这时，埋伏在河附近的瓦剌军从四面八方冲杀过来。明军丢盔弃甲，狂奔乱逃。英宗和王振带着一批禁军，几次想突围，都没能冲出去，王振也在混乱中被打死了。英宗眼看逃不出去，只好跳下马来。瓦剌兵冲上去，抓住了他。

[P16] 这次大战，明朝皇帝英宗被俘，六十六名大臣战死，死伤十多万名士兵，损失二十多万匹战马，最精锐的骑兵营、火枪营全军覆没。瓦剌军这招“擒贼擒王”，让明军失去指挥，乱成一团，彻底失败。瓦剌人抓去英宗，向明朝索要钱财，明朝也从此由盛转衰。
full_text_en:
[P1] Capture the bandit, capture the king.

[P2] In 1449, Emperor Yingzong of Ming suddenly received a report from the frontier, startling him so much that he slammed the table and stood up. His most trusted eunuch, Wang Zhen, seized the opportunity to say to him: 'Your Majesty, this is the perfect chance for you to show your mettle!'

'Reporting to Your Majesty, the Oirat leader Esen has led his troops to attack Datong, and General Wu Hao has been killed in battle!'

[P3] After hearing Wang Zhen's words, the Ming Yingzong made a shocking decision.
"I will lead the army in person and defeat the Wala!" Upon hearing this, the civil and military officials urged the Ming Yingzong not to risk a personal campaign.

[P4] "Your Majesty, border conflicts happen every year. If we send reinforcements and offer generous rewards, we can surely repel them. There's no need for Your Majesty to lead the campaign in person!"
"Your Majesty, the weather is now extremely hot. The grass has been scorched, and the rivers have dried up. If we send troops out, both men and horses will struggle for food and water. This is not a good time for a campaign!"
"Your Majesty, the Wala army came too suddenly. We are unprepared. It is far too risky for you to lead the campaign!"

[P5] But Emperor Yingzong was determined to achieve great feats, and no one could dissuade him. The imperial court hurriedly prepared. Two days before the army's departure, the court gave each soldier one tael of silver, a cotton coat, two pairs of shoes, and three dou of roasted wheat; they also emptied the armory and distributed over 800,000 weapons to the soldiers.
With so many supplies, if all were carried by soldiers, it would be impossible to march. So, the court assigned one small donkey to every three soldiers.

[P6] Everything was ready, and the Emperor Yingzong, accompanied by over a hundred civil and military officials, led a massive army of 200,000 troops, marching grandly from Beijing to the front lines. Since he didn't know how to fight, the Emperor entrusted all matters concerning marching and camping along the way to the eunuch Wang Zhen. Soon, the army arrived at the place called Xuanfu.
"Boom—" Suddenly, lightning flashed and thunder roared, strong winds blew people off balance, and large raindrops pattered down fiercely.

[P7] "Your Majesty, please rest in Xuanfu. We are willing to lead the troops to drive out the Oirats." The ministers, seeing the terrible weather, all pleaded with the emperor to halt his advance.
Wang Zhen, however, blocked them and angrily shouted: "The frontier has been in urgent danger multiple times. The Emperor, disregarding his own safety, is leading the troops in person. You are not going to inspect the camps, but instead want to hide from the wind and rain here? I have received a report: the Oirats have already retreated beyond the frontier. You should hurry and make battle plans!"

[P8] After marching in the rain for several days, the army finally arrived at Datong. However, the fires of battle had just died down, and everywhere were dead soldiers and wounded warhorses. The soldiers couldn't help but feel afraid upon seeing this scene.
At this moment, the military supervisor of Datong, Guo Jing, reported: "The Oirat commander Esen deliberately retreated, just to lure us forward. They have already set an ambush ahead. If we advance further, we will fall into their trap!"

[P9] That night, a heavy rain fell again in Datong. Wang Zhen dared no longer to advance and engage the Oirat army in battle. He quietly said to the Emperor Yingzong: "Your Majesty, along this route, it's either windy or raining. The weather is bad, and we cannot fight. Let's first return to the capital!" Seeing the corpses on the battlefield, the Emperor Yingzong was also frightened, and agreed to lead the troops back to Beijing the next day.

[P10] There are two routes from Datong back to Beijing: one is Zijing Pass, the other is Juyong Pass. Wang Zhen's eyes darted around, and he smiled at Emperor Yingzong, saying: "My hometown is in Yuizhou. If we return via Zijing Pass, we will pass right by. I humbly request Your Majesty to grace it with your presence and take a look!" Emperor Yingzong nodded and said: "Very well, you arrange it!"

[P11] The next day, the army set out early for Yuexiu.
But after traveling for a short while, Wang Zhen became worried again:
"So many people going to my home—won't they trample all my fields and crops?"
"Stop! Stop! Stop!" Wang Zhen quickly ordered the troops to halt,
then advised Emperor Yingzong, "After thinking it over, I believe the Emperor's safety must come first. The army should return to the capital via Juyong Pass, so we won't have to worry about being ambushed by the Oirats!"

[P12] Thus, the army changed course and headed toward Juyong Pass. This delay allowed the Oirat forces to catch up from behind. The Emperor hurriedly sent out 40,000 cavalry to block them, but unexpectedly, all 40,000 cavalry were annihilated by the Oirat army. They could only fight while retreating, eventually withdrawing all the way to Tumu Fort. Tumu Fort was built on a hill, a small fortress about 500 meters long and over 1,000 meters wide.

[P13] Chased by the Wala army for several days, the soldiers were parched with thirst. However, Tumu Fort had no well, and water had to be fetched from a small river fifteen li away. That river had already been occupied by the Wala army. The soldiers tried to dig a well, but even after digging one, two, or six to seven meters deep, not a single drop of water seeped out.
"Everyone, bear with it a little longer. Tomorrow, when we reach Xuanfu, we'll have water to drink," the generals comforted them.

[P14] The next day, as the army was about to set out, suddenly a soldier reported: "Bad news, there are Wala scouts outside, we've been surrounded!" The Wala scouts, having learned that the Ming army was numerous, soon withdrew. Upon hearing this, Wang Zhen hurriedly ordered the soldiers to go to the small river to water the horses and quench their thirst. The soldiers, starving and thirsty, rushed to the river in a frantic scramble, creating complete chaos.

[P15] At this moment, the Oirat troops hidden near the river charged in from all directions. The Ming army dropped their armor and fled in panic. Emperor Yingzong and Wang Zhen, leading a group of imperial guards, tried to break through several times but failed. Wang Zhen was killed in the chaos. Seeing no way out, Emperor Yingzong had to dismount. The Oirat soldiers rushed forward and captured him.

[P16] In this battle, the Ming Emperor Yingzong was captured, sixty-six ministers were killed, over 100,000 soldiers were killed or wounded, and more than 200,000 horses were lost. The most elite cavalry and arquebus units were completely annihilated. The Oirat army's tactic of 'capture the leader to capture the bandit' caused the Ming army to lose command, become chaotic, and suffer a total defeat. The Oirats took Emperor Yingzong captive and demanded money from the Ming dynasty, marking the beginning of the Ming's decline from prosperity.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页展示了绘本标题“擒贼擒王”，并配有一名身穿黄色龙袍、举手示意的帝王形象插图。
[P2] 本页描绘了公元1449年，明英宗接到边关战报后震惊不已，其宠信宦官王振趁机怂恿他亲征，同时有官员禀报瓦剌太师也先率军攻打大同、参将吴浩战死的消息。
[P3] 明英宗在宦官王振的怂恿下决定御驾亲征，文武百官听后纷纷劝阻，场面紧张。
[P4] 文武百官跪在殿前，纷纷劝阻明英宗不要御驾亲征，理由包括边境战事可派兵解决、天气炎热不利于行军、以及瓦剌军来势突然、准备不足等。
[P5] 本页描述了明英宗执意亲征后，朝廷匆忙为大军准备物资，包括发放银钱、衣物、粮食和大量兵器，并为士兵配备小毛驴以解决行军负担。
[P6] 明英宗率大军从北京出发亲征，因不谙军事，将行军扎营事务交由宦官王振管理，大军行至宣府时突遇狂风暴雨。
[P7] 明英宗亲征大军行至宣府时突遇暴雨，大臣们请求皇帝暂停前进并由他们率军出征，但宦官王振却怒斥他们，声称瓦剌已退，要求他们立即制定作战计划。
[P8] 明英宗亲征大军抵达大同，发现战场惨状，士兵心生畏惧。大同监军郭敬警告称瓦剌军故意退兵设伏，若继续前进将中计。
[P9] 明英宗亲征大军抵达大同后遭遇暴雨，王振劝说皇帝因天气恶劣且战场惨烈而班师回朝，英宗同意次日撤军。
[P10] 明英宗决定班师回朝，王振提议走紫荆关以便路过自己的家乡蔚州，英宗同意由王振安排撤军路线。
[P11] 明英宗亲征大军出发后，宦官王振因担心大军经过其家乡蔚州会踩坏庄稼，便以保障皇帝安全为由，建议大军改道经居庸关回京。
[P12] 明英宗亲征大军改道居庸关后，遭瓦剌军追击，派出的四万骑兵全军覆没，被迫一路后撤至土木堡。
[P13] 明英宗亲征大军被瓦剌军追击至土木堡，因无井且水源被占，士兵极度缺水，将领们安抚士兵称明日到宣府即可取水。
[P14] 大军准备出发时，士兵报告被瓦剌军包围，但瓦剌因明军人多而撤退。王振命将士去河边饮水，士兵因饥渴争抢，场面混乱。
[P15] 瓦剌军从河畔伏击明军，明军溃败，英宗与王振率禁军突围未果，王振被杀，英宗被俘。
[P16] 本页总结了土木堡之变的惨烈结局：明英宗被俘，大量官员和士兵阵亡，精锐部队覆灭，瓦剌军以‘擒贼擒王’之计致明军溃败，明朝从此由盛转衰。
